title: Non-Hermitian entropy production from fluctuation theorems
authors: Vasco Cavina, Frank Ernesto Quintela Rodríguez, Donato Farina
abstract: We develop a first-principles thermodynamic framework for non-Hermitian dynamics based on a post-selected version of the fluctuation theorem. This allows us to identify a quantity that remains positive throughout the non-Hermitian evolution and can be interpreted as the entropy production of the post-selected dynamics. We relate this quantity to previously proposed notions of non-Hermitian entropy and derive an associated second law. Furthermore, we establish a connection with information-theoretic quantities, in particular the Petz-Rényi divergences, and leverage this connection to derive upper and lower bounds. Finally, we decompose the entropy production into incoherent and coherent contributions, identifying distinctive features of the coherent term in the vicinity of exceptional points. We illustrate our results using a paradigmatic model of non-Hermitian evolution based on a two-level system.
summary: This paper establishes a thermodynamic framework for non-Hermitian quantum evolution by defining an entropy production quantity based on post-selected fluctuation theorems. The authors derive a generalized second law ($\langle\Delta Sangle + \Xi \ge 0$) and show that the coherent part of this production exhibits unique signatures, particularly near exceptional points in the system's parameter space.
main_problem: The authors develop a first-principles thermodynamic framework for non-Hermitian dynamics by identifying an entropy production quantity derived from a post-selected fluctuation theorem.
main_result: They establish a second law analogue, $\langle\Delta Sangle + \Xi \ge 0$, and show that the coherent contribution to entropy production ($\Xi_c$) exhibits distinctive signatures near exceptional points (EPs).
method: The framework utilizes post-selection on fluctuation theorems, relating entropy production ($\Sigma$) to information-theoretic measures like Petz–Rényi divergences ($D_2$).
model_or_system: The analysis is primarily conducted using a paradigmatic two-level system (qubit) governed by an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian $H_{	ext{eff}}(t)$.
key_observables: Entropy Production ($\Sigma$), Non-Hermitian Correction ($\Xi$), Average Entropy Variation ($\langle\Delta Sangle$), and the Coherent Contribution ($\Xi_c$).
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the behavior near Exceptional Points (EPs), where non-normality of the effective Hamiltonian becomes apparent.
main_assumptions: The framework relies fundamentally on post-selection, conditioning the dynamics on no jumps occurring during evolution.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the time evolution of $\Sigma$, $\Xi$, and $-\langle\Delta Sangle$ for a qubit model at an EP. Figure 2 specifically plots the coherent contribution $\Xi_c$ near the EP, showing a strongly negative signature centered exactly at the EP location.
paper_structure: The paper builds from deriving the formal definition of entropy production ($\Sigma$) using post-selected FTs, establishing its connection to relative entropies ($D_2$), and finally decomposing $\Sigma$ into incoherent and coherent parts to analyze EPs.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous thermodynamic interpretation for non-Hermitian quantum dynamics, linking concepts like entropy production and fluctuation theorems directly to spectral singularities (EPs), which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems.
